COMMON JUDGMENT
The Petitioners in MVC 4575/2020 & 1555/2021 have filed these petitions under Sec.166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation for the death of one Mukkandla Srinivasulu.

Both the petitions arose out of a common accident, therefore both the petitions are clubbed together as per order of the Hon'ble Chief Judge in Misc. No.42/2022 dated 14.03.2022, common evidence is recorded and common judgment is passed.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
These documents have not been seriously disputed by the Respondents.
The Respondents have not produced any contrary documents to dispute and rebut the contents of documents produced by the Petitioners.
As such, there are no reasons to discard the oral and documentary evidence produced by the Petitioners.
However, Petitioner Nos.2 & 3 4575/2020 being the sisters of the deceased are not legal heirs of the deceased.
Under such circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of Pws.1 & 2 and the documents, this court is of the opinion that the Petitioner Nos.1 in MVC 4575/2020 &
the petitioner in MVC 1555/2021 are the mother and wife of the deceased Mukkandla Srinivasulu.
The accident occurred in the year 2020.
Hence the same is considered as the monthly income of the deceased.
In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, the Petitioners have produced Aadhar Card of the deceased at Ex.P.8.
This is a public document and has got presumptive value under law.
In MVC 1555/2021 Petitioner i.e., wife of the deceased is considered as the dependent of the deceased.
As per the principles of law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma V/s  19 SCCH - 25 19 MVC Nos.4575/2020 &
 1555/2021 Delhi Transport Corporation, appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 14.
In the instant case, the deceased has a Mother and Wife, aged about 65 and 40 years respectively.
Therefore, they will be considered as the dependents of the deceased.
19. As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme court in National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others(AIR 2017 S.C 5157) persons aged above 60 years are not entitled to any future prospects.
20 . This observation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is reaffirmed in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd.
 21 SCCH - 25 21 MVC Nos.4575/2020 &
 1555/2021 Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021)
11 SCC 780.
 21.
The loss of a Son and Husband full of hopes for the future can never be suitably compensated to the parents and spouse.
However, both are entitled to a sum of Rs.88,000/- (Rs.44,000/- each) under the head of loss of consortium.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, in the interest of justice the Petitioners in both the cases are awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
Therefore, the Petitioners in both the cases are entitled for Rs.20,000/- under the head of loss of estate.
Therefore, the Petitioner No.1 in MVC 4575/2020 and the petitioner in MVC 1555/2021 are entitled for a total sum of Rs.21,58,112/-.
If it is rounded off then comes to Varalakshmi vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78496210/
16 Rs.21,58,200/-.
 LIABILITY:
 22.
The respondent did not prove their defence.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The respondent  23 SCCH - 25 23 MVC Nos.4575/2020 &
 1555/2021 insurance company of Goods Carrier Lorry is liable to indemnify the respondent Owner.
The petitioners in MVC No.4575/2020 have claimed for a sum of Rs.50,00,000/-
and the petitioner in MVC No.1555/2021 has claimed for a sum of Rs.50,00,000/- but they are jointly entitled only for a sum of Rs.21,58,200/- with interest @6% per annum from the date of petition of MVC 4575/2020 till its realization.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly, issue No.3 in MVC No.4575/2020 and MVC No.1555/2021 are held in the Affirmative.
23. Issue No.3 & 4 in all the cases:
For the reasons and discussions made above and  findings to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to  pass the following:-
 ORDER
The petitions in MVC No.4575/2020 & MVC No.1555/2021 are hereby allowed with cost.
SCCH - 25 24 MVC Nos.4575/2020 & 1555/2021 The Respondent Nos.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
However, the Respondent insurer is liable to indemnify the Respondent RC owner and directed to deposit the compensation amount to the Petitioners within 60 days from today.
The Petitioner No.1 in MVC No.4575/2020 and petitioner in MVC 1555/2021 are entitled for a sum of Rs.21,58,200/- (Rupees Twenty One Lakhs Fifty Eight Thousand and Two Hundred only) with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of filing of MVC 4575/2020 till the date of depositing the award amount.
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire amount shall be released equally to the petitioner No.1 in MVC 4575/2020 and petitioner in MVC 1555/2021 SCCH - 25 25 MVC Nos.4575/2020 &
1555/2021 by way of e-payment with due acknowledgment and proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/- in each case.
The original copy of this judgment is ordered to be kept in MVC No.4575/2020 and copy shall be kept in MVC No.1555/2021.
